newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Fyffes confident about future prospects.
newsitem.headline: Fyffes confident about future prospects.

text.p: Irish fruit and vegetable importer and wholesaler Fyffes Plc said on Wednesday that it was confident about the future prospects for the group.
"Going into the latter half of the year, trading conditions are similar to those that prevailed in the second six months of last year," the group said in its half-year results statement.
Earlier Fyffes announced a 2.6 percent drop in pre-tax profits to 20.2 million Irish pounds while operating profits slipped by 3.7 percent to 18.8 million.

The company had warned at its annual meeting that first-half results might be down on last year but noted that although the actual outcome showed a drop in profits, earnings per share rose by five percent on an adjusted basis.
Fyffes blamed the drop in operating profits on lower average selling prices in the first half resulting from higher than normal supply volues across a wide range of produce.
"An additional significant factor was the strengthening of the Irish pound and the U.S. dollar against continental European currencies by 12 percent and 15 percent respectively," it said.
But the group said its strong balance sheet and cashflow left it well palced to take the business forward and that it continued to pursue an active acquisition programme.
Net cash at April 30 was 49.1 million punts against 19.0 million a year earlier while shareholders fund srose by 17 percent to 215.3 million.

The improved cash position reflects the continuing strong cashflow from the group's operations and reduced working capital requirements compared to the first half of 1996 while the increase in shareholders funds was helped by the strength of sterling.
Fyffes said earlier that it was buying 50 percent of Dutch fresh produce group Velleman & Tas for a total consideration of 22.2 million Irish pounds.
